title: Denied hostname lookups reach the resolver because a Squid IP exception resolves names
symptoms: Resolver or DNS-policy logs show lookups for a hostname the agent was denied (TCP_DENIED / 403) in default mode
A hostname is refused by Squid but its name still appears in DNS telemetry
conditions: The generated squid.conf contains a destination-IP ACL declared as dst without -n: an API-proxy or explicit-IP exception (allow_api_proxy_ip, allow_ip_*), the TLS SNI guard (tls_sni_guard_allowed_ip), or an API-proxy upstream, broker splice or broker logging ACL for an IP-literal endpoint
The ACL is evaluated before the domain deny or in a splice/logging decision, so Squid may resolve the requested hostname to test it against the IP
Direct DNS queries from the agent, and lookups of allowlisted names, are outside this finding; they are governed by the trusted --dns-servers policy (NET-002)
rootCause: A Squid dst ACL without -n resolves a hostname destination before matching it against an IP, so evaluating the exception ahead of the domain deny issued a DNS query for an unlisted name even though HTTP access was then refused. dst -n matches literal IPs only, so a hostname is never resolved and does not inherit the IP exception. Current main emits dst -n for the API-proxy and explicit-IP exceptions (config-sections.ts), the SSL-bump SNI guard (ssl-bump.ts) and IP-literal API-proxy upstream, broker splice and broker logging ACLs (api-proxy-upstreams.ts); hostname upstreams use dstdom_regex -i -n instead. The emitter changes were verified only by generated-configuration tests, not by observing Squid lookups, and the release range containing them is unknown.

probe.expect: Every matched ACL line carries -n (for example 'dst -n 172.30.0.30'), including TLS SNI guard and broker access, splice and logging ACLs. A line without -n identifies an unscoped destination-IP ACL. This checks emitted configuration only, not runtime lookup behavior; no traffic is sent and no credentials or environment are read. Redact paths before sharing.

action: Use source containing numeric-only (dst -n) API-proxy and explicit-IP exceptions and regenerate the configuration. Keep the domain allowlist, raw-IP deny rules and rule ordering unchanged, and do not widen the allowlist or disable DNS filtering. This does not filter direct DNS queries or lookups of allowlisted names; use a policy-enforcing resolver through --dns-servers if those need control. If a denied name reaches the resolver with the fixed ACLs in place, escalate with redacted evidence under SEC-001 instead of reproducing it publicly.
